entities.summary:
Isetemkheb D was the sister-wife of the Theban High Priest of Amun Pinedjem II during the Twenty-first Dynasty of Egypt. Her marriage to Pinedjem II is documented in several ancient Egyptian texts, including the Turin Royal Canon and the Harris Papyrus.

As the sister-wife of a high-ranking priest, Isetemkheb D would have played an important role in the religious and administrative life of Thebes during this period. Her position may also have provided her with access to significant wealth and power.

The exact dates of Isetemkheb D's life are unknown, but it is believed that she lived during the reign of Pinedjem II (c. 1050-1018 BCE).

Isetemkheb D's legacy may be seen in the continued worship of Amun and the preservation of ancient Egyptian traditions during this period.

A testament to her enduring impact, Isetemkheb D remains an important figure in the study of ancient Egyptian history and culture.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As the sister-wife of Pinedjem II, Isetemkheb D played a significant role in Theban politics and society during the Twenty-first Dynasty of Egypt. Her marriage to Pinedjem II helped solidify his position as High Priest and contributed to the continued worship of Amun and the preservation of ancient Egyptian traditions.
